| `qyl.agent.record.payload` | any | recommended | Not applicable | development | Optional original source record retained for explicitly enabled diagnostics. |
| `qyl.agent.source` | enum | recommended | Not applicable | development | Collection boundary from which an observation was obtained. |
| `qyl.agent.turn.id` | string | recommended | Not applicable | development | Native turn or prompt identifier scoped to its provider and conversation. |

#### Attribute details: `qyl.agent.operation.id`

An adapter MUST reuse this identifier across the operation's lifecycle and retries of record delivery.
Use a source-provided invocation ID scoped by product, workspace and session, with one documented
mapping shared by observers. A per-event record ID, fresh random value or timestamp is not an operation
identity. When the source does not establish an operation identity, retain the source record without
inventing an operation entity or lifecycle. This high-cardinality identifier belongs on events and spans,
not metrics. Reconcile equivalent observations across sources before counting the same operation twice.


Examples: `["openai:workspace-7:thread-42:call-9"]`.

#### Attribute details: `qyl.agent.operation.name`

A model retry remains a separate request attempt within its enclosing turn. Record daily aggregates as aggregates, not fabricated operations.

| Member | Wire value | Stability | Meaning / deprecation |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `turn` | `turn` | development | One agent turn. |
| `model_request` | `model_request` | development | One model request attempt. |
| `tool` | `tool` | development | One tool invocation. |
| `approval` | `approval` | development | One approval decision cycle. |
| `task` | `task` | development | One explicitly identified background or cloud task. |

#### Attribute details: `qyl.agent.operation.state`

Missing telemetry does not imply completion or failure. Approval denial, process exit, tool completion
and turn completion are different facts. Map a source outcome only within the operation it describes.
This is descriptive entity state and MUST NOT be part of entity identity.


| Member | Wire value | Stability | Meaning / deprecation |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `queued` | `queued` | development | Accepted and waiting to start. |
| `running` | `running` | development | Execution has started. |
| `waiting` | `waiting` | development | Explicitly waiting for an external decision or dependency. |
| `completed` | `completed` | development | Completed successfully according to the source. |
| `failed` | `failed` | development | Failed according to the source. |
| `cancelled` | `cancelled` | development | Explicitly cancelled or interrupted. |
| `unknown` | `unknown` | development | Current state cannot be established from available observations. |

#### Attribute details: `qyl.agent.parent.operation.id`

Record only when the source establishes the parent. Temporal proximity or matching model names do not establish ancestry.

Examples: `["openai:workspace-7:thread-42:turn-3"]`.

#### Attribute details: `qyl.agent.product`

This is product attribution, not the underlying model provider. For example, Codex may use a configured non-OpenAI model provider.

| Member | Wire value | Stability | Meaning / deprecation |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `codex` | `codex` | development | Codex execution. |
| `chatgpt` | `chatgpt` | development | ChatGPT activity. |
| `claude_code` | `claude_code` | development | Claude Code execution. |
| `cowork` | `cowork` | development | Cowork execution. |
| `claude` | `claude` | development | Other documented Claude activity. |

#### Attribute details: `qyl.agent.record.id`

Deduplicate at-least-once delivery using source stream/workspace plus this value. OpenAI compliance event_id is suitable in its documented stream scope; a timestamp alone is not.

Examples: `["event-123"]`.

#### Attribute details: `qyl.agent.record.observed_at`

Keep the original event time on the event timestamp. This field measures collection delay and does not replace source time.

Examples: `["2026-10-18T06:00:00.000Z"]`.

#### Attribute details: `qyl.agent.record.payload`

May contain conversation content, commands, personal identifiers and secrets. Omit by default. Apply
redaction, access controls and a configured byte limit before export. Preserve a separate external
reference when truncation would make the record unusable. Never place this value on a metric.


Attribute annotations:

```json
{
  "type": {
    "json_schema": {
      "type": "object"
    }
  },
  "value": {
    "unbounded_size": true
  }
}
```

#### Attribute details: `qyl.agent.source`

Private product analytics declarations are evidence about a product, not authorization or a supported ingestion route.

| Member | Wire value | Stability | Meaning / deprecation |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `otlp` | `otlp` | development | Native OTLP observation. |
| `compliance` | `compliance` | development | Published compliance record. |
| `analytics` | `analytics` | development | Published aggregate analytics record. |
| `local_diagnostic` | `local_diagnostic` | development | Explicitly collected local diagnostic. |

#### Attribute details: `qyl.agent.turn.id`

Codex turn.id and Claude prompt.id can populate this field when their source contracts identify the
request being observed. Do not equate a conversation, a model request and a turn. Turn IDs can be absent.


Examples: `["turn-3"]`.


### span.qyl.agent.operation.internal

One observed agent operation, with explicitly established start and end boundaries.

| Property | Definition |
| --- | --- |
| Kind | `span` |
| Stability | development |
| Signal collection | recommended |
| span_kind | `internal` |
| Registry schema | https://qyl.at/schemas/15.0.1 |
| Source | `registry/qyl/agent-observability.yaml` |

Start when the source establishes that this operation begins; end on its matching terminal observation.
A retry of a model request is a child attempt, not a new whole turn. Do not synthesize a span from a daily
analytics row or a lone completion record with unknown start time. Preserve native spans when available
instead of creating duplicate wrapper spans. The low-cardinality span name is `agent {qyl.agent.operation.name}`.
Set Error status only for an established operation failure, with error.type. Expected cancellation or denied
approval is not automatically an error. Leave successful status Unset. Do not put identifiers in span names.
Product, operation category and established identity are available at start; state, duration and error facts
become available at completion and cannot be assumed present for head sampling.


| Attribute | Type | Requirement / role | Sampling relevant | Stability | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `error.type` | enum | {"conditionally_required":"If the observed operation failed."} | false | stable | Describes a class of error the operation ended with.  The `error.type` SHOULD be predictable, and SHOULD have low cardinality.  When `error.type` is set to a type (e.g., an exception type), its canonical class name identifying the type within the artifact SHOULD be used.  If the recorded error type is a wrapper that is not meaningful for failure classification, instrumentation MAY use the type of the inner error instead. For example, in Go, errors created with `fmt.Errorf` using `%w` MAY be unwrapped when the wrapper type does not help classify the failure.  Instrumentations SHOULD document the list of errors they report.  The cardinality of `error.type` within one instrumentation library SHOULD be low. Telemetry consumers that aggregate data from multiple instrumentation libraries and applications should be prepared for `error.type` to have high cardinality at query time when no additional filters are applied.  If the operation has completed successfully, instrumentations SHOULD NOT set `error.type`.  If a specific domain defines its own set of error identifiers (such as HTTP or RPC status codes), it's RECOMMENDED to:  - Use a domain-specific attribute - Set `error.type` to capture all errors, regardless of whether they are defined within the domain-specific set or not.  |
| `gen_ai.conversation.id` | string | recommended | false | development | The unique identifier for a conversation (session, thread), used to store and correlate messages within this conversation. Instrumentations SHOULD populate conversation id when they have an identifier for the conversation readily available for a given operation, for example:  - when the client framework being instrumented manages conversation history (see [LlamaIndex chat store](https://docs.llamaindex.ai/en/stable/module_guides/storing/chat_stores/), [LangChain `session_id`](https://reference.langchain.com/python/langchain-core/runnables/history/RunnableWithMessageHistory), and [Google ADK sessions](https://adk.dev/sessions/session)) - when instrumenting GenAI client libraries that maintain a conversation on the backend (see [AWS Bedrock agent sessions](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/agents-session-state.html), [OpenAI Assistant threads](https://platform.openai.com/docs/api-reference/threads))  When no identifier for the conversation is available, instrumentations SHOULD NOT populate conversation id. For example, a new UUID, a trace identifier, or a hash of request content SHOULD NOT be used as a fallback value.  Application developers that manage conversation history MAY add conversation id to GenAI and other spans or logs using custom span or log record processors or hooks provided by instrumentation libraries.  |
| `gen_ai.tool.call.id` | string | recommended | false | development | The tool call identifier supplied by the model or provider. This attribute SHOULD be set to the identifier received from the model or provider if and only if one was supplied.  |
| `qyl.agent.operation.id` | string | required | false | development | Stable identifier for one observed logical operation. An adapter MUST reuse this identifier across the operation's lifecycle and retries of record delivery. Use a source-provided invocation ID scoped by product, workspace and session, with one documented mapping shared by observers. A per-event record ID, fresh random value or timestamp is not an operation identity. When the source does not establish an operation identity, retain the source record without inventing an operation entity or lifecycle. This high-cardinality identifier belongs on events and spans, not metrics. Reconcile equivalent observations across sources before counting the same operation twice.  |
| `qyl.agent.operation.name` | enum | required | false | development | Bounded operation category used for cross-producer comparisons. A model retry remains a separate request attempt within its enclosing turn. Record daily aggregates as aggregates, not fabricated operations. |
| `qyl.agent.operation.state` | enum | recommended | false | development | Last established lifecycle state of an operation. |
| `qyl.agent.parent.operation.id` | string | recommended | false | development | Identifier of the directly enclosing observed operation. Record only when the source establishes the parent. Temporal proximity or matching model names do not establish ancestry. |
| `qyl.agent.product` | enum | required | false | development | Product responsible for the observed activity. This is product attribution, not the underlying model provider. For example, Codex may use a configured non-OpenAI model provider. |

| `qyl.agent.turn.id` | string | recommended | false | development | Native turn or prompt identifier scoped to its provider and conversation. Codex turn.id and Claude prompt.id can populate this field when their source contracts identify the request being observed. Do not equate a conversation, a model request and a turn. Turn IDs can be absent.  |

#### Attribute details: `qyl.api.contract.revision`

A resource-level attribute: one value per process, carried on the resource rather than written per span, so every signal the process emits carries it and no hot path touches it. It is computed at build time, not at startup: `Qyl.Api.Sdk`'s build targets run MSBuild's `GetFileHash` over the committed `openapi/<app>.json` and compile the resulting `sha256:<hex>` in as a constant, which `AddQylApi` stamps onto the resource. It answers which contract revision a running process was built from, so a response that disagrees with the published document is traced to a build rather than guessed at from a deployment.

Examples: `["sha256:264a9e4f1d70289a3b5c6e8f0a1d2c4b7e9f13058a6cd2ef4b91073d5c8e6a2f"]`.

#### Attribute details: `qyl.attribute.namespace`

The value set is closed and is exactly the attribute namespaces present in the resolved registry plus `other`: the collector clamps every value it records to this set, so an inbound payload carrying an unknown key cannot fork the series. `registry/policies-v2/qyl_attribute_namespace.rego` recomputes the set from the resolved catalog on every `weaver registry check` and fails it when the two disagree, so a registry that gains a namespace cannot silently leave it unlisted.

#### Attribute details: `qyl.gen_ai.tool.call.arguments_hash`

Staging: upstream semantic conventions have no argument fingerprint attribute. Compare only within the same producer and project; hashes with different canonicalization or keys are not comparable. Producers should use a keyed cryptographic hash and must not place raw arguments in this field. Absence means repeated arguments are unknown.


Examples: `["5c74502b204fa7d66a0d03caf5c15960be740acd30631161095791aa8f5c47c8"]`.

### metric.qyl.qyl_collector_attributes_coalesced

Identical typed duplicate attributes coalesced into one map entry at ingest.

| Property | Definition |
| --- | --- |
| Kind | `metric` |
| Stability | development |
| Signal collection | recommended |
| metric_name | `qyl.collector.attributes.coalesced` |
| instrument | `counter` |
| unit | `{attribute}` |
| Registry schema | https://qyl.at/schemas/15.0.1 |
| Source | `registry/qyl/metrics.yaml` |

For example, an ILogger message and its activity scope can export the same TraceId. Only identical values are coalesced; conflicting duplicate values are rejected explicitly. Count by a bounded namespace and never record the value.

| Attribute | Type | Requirement / role | Sampling relevant | Stability | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `qyl.attribute.namespace` | enum | required | Not applicable | development | First dot-segment of the attribute key a collector measurement is about. The value set is closed and is exactly the attribute namespaces present in the resolved registry plus `other`: the collector clamps every value it records to this set, so an inbound payload carrying an unknown key cannot fork the series. `registry/policies-v2/qyl_attribute_namespace.rego` recomputes the set from the resolved catalog on every `weaver registry check` and fails it when the two disagree, so a registry that gains a namespace cannot silently leave it unlisted. |

### metric.qyl.qyl_collector_attributes_sanitization_failed

Exception attributes replaced with a safe marker because their value could not be sanitized.

| Property | Definition |
| --- | --- |
| Kind | `metric` |
| Stability | development |
| Signal collection | recommended |
| metric_name | `qyl.collector.attributes.sanitization.failed` |
| instrument | `counter` |
| unit | `{attribute}` |
| Registry schema | https://qyl.at/schemas/15.0.1 |
| Source | `registry/qyl/metrics.yaml` |

The Collector records only the bounded attribute key and failure category. Attribute values, captured credentials and sanitizer exception text never appear in this diagnostic.

| Attribute | Type | Requirement / role | Sampling relevant | Stability | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `error.type` | enum | required | Not applicable | stable | Describes a class of error the operation ended with.  The `error.type` SHOULD be predictable, and SHOULD have low cardinality.  When `error.type` is set to a type (e.g., an exception type), its canonical class name identifying the type within the artifact SHOULD be used.  If the recorded error type is a wrapper that is not meaningful for failure classification, instrumentation MAY use the type of the inner error instead. For example, in Go, errors created with `fmt.Errorf` using `%w` MAY be unwrapped when the wrapper type does not help classify the failure.  Instrumentations SHOULD document the list of errors they report.  The cardinality of `error.type` within one instrumentation library SHOULD be low. Telemetry consumers that aggregate data from multiple instrumentation libraries and applications should be prepared for `error.type` to have high cardinality at query time when no additional filters are applied.  If the operation has completed successfully, instrumentations SHOULD NOT set `error.type`.  If a specific domain defines its own set of error identifiers (such as HTTP or RPC status codes), it's RECOMMENDED to:  - Use a domain-specific attribute - Set `error.type` to capture all errors, regardless of whether they are defined within the domain-specific set or not.  |
| `qyl.attribute.key` | enum | required | Not applicable | development | The bounded exception attribute key associated with a value-sanitization failure. |

#### Attribute details: `db.query.summary`

The query summary describes a class of database queries and is useful
as a grouping key, especially when analyzing telemetry for database
calls involving complex queries.

Summary may be available to the instrumentation through
instrumentation hooks or other means. If it is not available, instrumentations
that support query parsing SHOULD generate a summary following
[Generating query summary](/docs/db/database-spans.md#generating-a-summary-of-the-query)
section.

For batch operations, if the individual operations are known to have the same query summary
then that query summary SHOULD be used prepended by `BATCH `,
otherwise `db.query.summary` SHOULD be `BATCH` or some other database
system specific term if more applicable.


Examples: `["SELECT wuser_table","INSERT shipping_details SELECT orders","get user by id"]`.

Attribute annotations:

```json
{
  "qyl": {
    "token_exempt": true
  }
}
```

#### Attribute details: `db.query.text`

For sanitization see [Sanitization of `db.query.text`](/docs/db/database-spans.md#sanitization-of-dbquerytext).
For batch operations, if the individual operations are known to have the same query text then that query text SHOULD be used, otherwise all of the individual query texts SHOULD be concatenated with separator `; ` or some other database system specific separator if more applicable.
Parameterized query text SHOULD NOT be sanitized. Even though parameterized query text can potentially have sensitive data, by using a parameterized query the user is giving a strong signal that any sensitive data will be passed as parameter values, and the benefit to observability of capturing the static part of the query text by default outweighs the risk.


Examples: `["SELECT * FROM wuser_table where username = ?","SET mykey ?"]`.

Attribute annotations:

```json
{
  "qyl": {
    "persisted": false
  }
}
```

#### Attribute details: `gen_ai.conversation.id`

Instrumentations SHOULD populate conversation id when they have an identifier
for the conversation readily available for a given operation, for example:

- when the client framework being instrumented manages conversation history
(see [LlamaIndex chat store](https://docs.llamaindex.ai/en/stable/module_guides/storing/chat_stores/),
[LangChain `session_id`](https://reference.langchain.com/python/langchain-core/runnables/history/RunnableWithMessageHistory),
and [Google ADK sessions](https://adk.dev/sessions/session))
- when instrumenting GenAI client libraries that maintain a conversation on the backend
(see [AWS Bedrock agent sessions](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/agents-session-state.html),
[OpenAI Assistant threads](https://platform.openai.com/docs/api-reference/threads))

When no identifier for the conversation is available, instrumentations SHOULD NOT
populate conversation id. For example, a new UUID, a trace identifier, or a hash
of request content SHOULD NOT be used as a fallback value.

Application developers that manage conversation history MAY add conversation id to GenAI and other
spans or logs using custom span or log record processors or hooks provided by instrumentation
libraries.


Examples: `["conv_5j66UpCpwteGg4YSxUnt7lPY"]`.

```json
    "persisted": false
  }
}
```

#### Attribute details: `gen_ai.data_source.id`

Data sources are used by AI agents and RAG applications to store grounding data. A data source may be an external database, object store, document collection, website, or any other storage system used by the GenAI agent or application. The `gen_ai.data_source.id` SHOULD match the identifier used by the GenAI system rather than a name specific to the external storage, such as a database or object store. Semantic conventions referencing `gen_ai.data_source.id` MAY also leverage additional attributes, such as `db.*`, to further identify and describe the data source.


Examples: `["H7STPQYOND"]`.

#### Attribute details: `gen_ai.output.messages`

Each message represents a single output choice/candidate generated by
the model. Each message corresponds to exactly one generation
(choice/candidate) and vice versa - one choice cannot be split across
multiple messages or one message cannot contain parts from multiple choices.

Instrumentations MAY provide a way for users to filter or truncate
output messages. `gen_ai.response.finish_reasons` remains aligned with the
generations returned by the provider, not with a filtered or truncated
`gen_ai.output.messages` value.

When an operation ends in an error, this attribute SHOULD only be set
when the operation produced output, including partial streamed output.
Instrumentation SHOULD NOT synthesize output content for a failed
operation.

> [!Warning]
> This attribute is likely to contain sensitive information including user/PII data.

See [Recording content on attributes](/docs/gen-ai/gen-ai-spans.md#recording-content-on-attributes)
section for more details.


Examples: `["[\n  {\n    \"role\": \"assistant\",\n    \"parts\": [\n      {\n        \"type\": \"text\",\n        \"content\": \"The weather in Paris is currently rainy with a temperature of 57°F.\"\n      }\n    ]\n  }\n]\n"]`.

Attribute annotations:

```json
{
  "qyl": {
    "persisted": false
  }
}
```

This value SHOULD include all types of input tokens, including cached tokens.
Instrumentations SHOULD make a best effort to populate this value, using a total
provided by the provider when available or, depending on the provider API,
by summing different token types parsed from the provider output.

When the provider reports both billed token counts and model-consumed
token counts (for example, Cohere exposes both `usage.billed_units` and
`usage.tokens`), instrumentations SHOULD report the billed count so the
value matches the units the customer is charged for.

Detailed usage attributes are subsets of total and aggregate counts. For example,
if a request has 100 text tokens (40 cached) and 200 image tokens:
- `gen_ai.usage.input_tokens`: 300
- `gen_ai.usage.cache_read.input_tokens`: 40
- `gen_ai.usage.text.input_tokens`: 100
- `gen_ai.usage.text.cache_read.input_tokens`: 40
- `gen_ai.usage.image.input_tokens`: 200


Examples: `[100]`.

Attribute annotations:

```json
{
  "qyl": {
    "token_exempt": true
  }
}
```

#### Attribute details: `gen_ai.usage.output_tokens`

When the provider reports both billed token counts and model-consumed
token counts (for example, Cohere exposes both `usage.billed_units` and
`usage.tokens`), instrumentations SHOULD report the billed count so the
value matches the units the customer is charged for.


Examples: `[180]`.

Attribute annotations:

```json
{
  "qyl": {
    "token_exempt": true
  }
}
```

#### Attribute details: `gen_ai.workflow.name`

The workflow name is usually a static, application-unique identifier defined
in a framework-specific way.

For example, it can be the name of the first chain in LangChain,
the name of the crew in CrewAI, or the entry point agent in ADK or
OpenAI Agents when no explicit workflow name is provided.

This attribute MUST have low cardinality. It is NOT RECOMMENDED to use
instrumentation-time constants or names of types representing the workflow,
such as "StateGraph". When no meaningful, low-cardinality workflow name is
available for a given framework, this attribute MUST NOT be captured by default.

Semantic conventions for individual Generative AI frameworks SHOULD document
what `gen_ai.workflow.name` means in the context of that framework.


Examples: `["multi_agent_rag","customer_support_pipeline"]`.

#### Attribute details: `service.instance.id`

MUST be unique for each instance of the same `service.namespace,service.name` pair (in other words
`service.namespace,service.name,service.instance.id` triplet MUST be globally unique). The ID helps to
distinguish instances of the same service that exist at the same time (e.g. instances of a horizontally scaled
service).

Implementations, such as SDKs, are recommended to generate a random Version 1 or Version 4 [RFC
4122](https://www.ietf.org/rfc/rfc4122.txt) UUID, but are free to use an inherent unique ID as the source of
this value if stability is desirable. In that case, the ID SHOULD be used as source of a UUID Version 5 and
SHOULD use the following UUID as the namespace: `4d63009a-8d0f-11ee-aad7-4c796ed8e320`.

UUIDs are typically recommended, as only an opaque value for the purposes of identifying a service instance is
needed. Similar to what can be seen in the man page for the
[`/etc/machine-id`](https://www.freedesktop.org/software/systemd/man/latest/machine-id.html) file, the underlying
data, such as pod name and namespace should be treated as confidential, being the user's choice to expose it
or not via another resource attribute.

For applications running behind an application server (like unicorn), we do not recommend using one identifier
for all processes participating in the application. Instead, it's recommended each division (e.g. a worker
thread in unicorn) to have its own instance.id.

It's not recommended for a Collector to set `service.instance.id` if it can't unambiguously determine the
service instance that is generating that telemetry. For instance, creating an UUID based on `pod.name` will
likely be wrong, as the Collector might not know from which container within that pod the telemetry originated.
However, Collectors can set the `service.instance.id` if they can unambiguously determine the service instance
for that telemetry. This is typically the case for scraping receivers, as they know the target address and
port.


Examples: `["627cc493-f310-47de-96bd-71410b7dec09"]`.

Attribute annotations:

```json
{
  "qyl": {
    "persisted": false
  }
}
```

#### Attribute details: `url.full`

For network calls, URL usually has `scheme://host[:port][path][?query][#fragment]` format, where the fragment
is not transmitted over HTTP, but if it is known, it SHOULD be included nevertheless.

`url.full` MUST NOT contain credentials passed via URL in form of `https://username:password@www.example.com/`.
In such case username and password SHOULD be redacted and attribute's value SHOULD be `https://REDACTED:REDACTED@www.example.com/`.

`url.full` SHOULD capture the absolute URL when it is available (or can be reconstructed).

Sensitive content provided in `url.full` SHOULD be scrubbed when instrumentations can identify it.

![Development](https://img.shields.io/badge/-development-blue)
Query string values for the following keys SHOULD be redacted by default and replaced by the
value `REDACTED`:

* [`X-Amz-Signature`](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/IAM/latest/UserGuide/reference_sigv-authentication-methods.html)
* [`X-Amz-Credential`](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/IAM/latest/UserGuide/reference_sigv-authentication-methods.html)
* [`X-Amz-Security-Token`](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/IAM/latest/UserGuide/reference_sigv-authentication-methods.html)
* [`sig`](https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/storage/common/storage-sas-overview#sas-token)
* [`X-Goog-Signature`](https://cloud.google.com/storage/docs/access-control/signed-urls)

This list is subject to change over time.

Matching of query parameter keys against the sensitive list SHOULD be case-sensitive.

![Development](https://img.shields.io/badge/-development-blue)
Instrumentation MAY provide a way to override this list via declarative configuration.
If so, it SHOULD use the `sensitive_query_parameters` property
(an array of case-sensitive strings with minimum items 0) under
`.instrumentation/development.general.sanitization.url`.
This list is a full override of the default sensitive query parameter keys,
it is not a list of keys in addition to the defaults.

When a query string value is redacted, the query string key SHOULD still be preserved, e.g.
`https://www.example.com/path?color=blue&sig=REDACTED`.


Examples: `["https://www.foo.bar/search?q=OpenTelemetry#SemConv","//localhost"]`.

Attribute annotations:

```json
{
  "qyl": {
    "persisted": false
  }
}
```

#### Attribute details: `url.query`

Sensitive content provided in `url.query` SHOULD be scrubbed when instrumentations can identify it.

![Development](https://img.shields.io/badge/-development-blue)
Query string values for the following keys SHOULD be redacted by default and replaced by the value `REDACTED`:

* [`X-Amz-Signature`](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/IAM/latest/UserGuide/reference_sigv-authentication-methods.html)
* [`X-Amz-Credential`](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/IAM/latest/UserGuide/reference_sigv-authentication-methods.html)
* [`X-Amz-Security-Token`](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/IAM/latest/UserGuide/reference_sigv-authentication-methods.html)
* [`sig`](https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/storage/common/storage-sas-overview#sas-token)
* [`X-Goog-Signature`](https://cloud.google.com/storage/docs/access-control/signed-urls)

This list is subject to change over time.

Matching of query parameter keys against the sensitive list SHOULD be case-sensitive.

Instrumentation MAY provide a way to override this list via declarative configuration.
If so, it SHOULD use the `sensitive_query_parameters` property
(an array of case-sensitive strings with minimum items 0) under
`.instrumentation/development.general.sanitization.url`.
This list is a full override of the default sensitive query parameter keys,
it is not a list of keys in addition to the defaults.

When a query string value is redacted, the query string key SHOULD still be preserved, e.g.
`q=OpenTelemetry&sig=REDACTED`.


Examples: `["q=OpenTelemetry"]`.

Attribute annotations:

```json
{
  "qyl": {
    "persisted": false
  }
}
```

#### Attribute details: `db.response.status_code`

The status code returned by the database. Usually it represents an error code, but may also represent partial success, warning, or differentiate between various types of successful outcomes.
Semantic conventions for individual database systems SHOULD document what `db.response.status_code` means in the context of that system.


Examples: `["102","ORA-17002","08P01","404"]`.

Attribute annotations:

```json
{
  "qyl": {
    "phase": "end"
  }
}
```

#### Attribute details: `error.type`

The `error.type` SHOULD be predictable, and SHOULD have low cardinality.

When `error.type` is set to a type (e.g., an exception type), its
canonical class name identifying the type within the artifact SHOULD be used.

If the recorded error type is a wrapper that is not meaningful for
failure classification, instrumentation MAY use the type of the inner
error instead. For example, in Go, errors created with `fmt.Errorf`
using `%w` MAY be unwrapped when the wrapper type does not help
classify the failure.

Instrumentations SHOULD document the list of errors they report.

The cardinality of `error.type` within one instrumentation library SHOULD be low.
Telemetry consumers that aggregate data from multiple instrumentation libraries and applications
should be prepared for `error.type` to have high cardinality at query time when no
additional filters are applied.

If the operation has completed successfully, instrumentations SHOULD NOT set `error.type`.

If a specific domain defines its own set of error identifiers (such as HTTP or RPC status codes),
it's RECOMMENDED to:

- Use a domain-specific attribute
- Set `error.type` to capture all errors, regardless of whether they are defined within the domain-specific set or not.


Examples: `["timeout","java.net.UnknownHostException","server_certificate_invalid","500"]`.

| Member | Wire value | Stability | Meaning / deprecation |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `other` | `_OTHER` | stable | A fallback error value to be used when the instrumentation doesn't define a custom value.  |

Attribute annotations:

```json
{
  "qyl": {
    "phase": "end"
  }
}
```

#### Attribute details: `gen_ai.output.messages`

Each message represents a single output choice/candidate generated by
the model. Each message corresponds to exactly one generation
(choice/candidate) and vice versa - one choice cannot be split across
multiple messages or one message cannot contain parts from multiple choices.

Instrumentations MAY provide a way for users to filter or truncate
output messages. `gen_ai.response.finish_reasons` remains aligned with the
generations returned by the provider, not with a filtered or truncated
`gen_ai.output.messages` value.

When an operation ends in an error, this attribute SHOULD only be set
when the operation produced output, including partial streamed output.
Instrumentation SHOULD NOT synthesize output content for a failed
operation.

> [!Warning]
> This attribute is likely to contain sensitive information including user/PII data.

See [Recording content on attributes](/docs/gen-ai/gen-ai-spans.md#recording-content-on-attributes)
section for more details.


Examples: `["[\n  {\n    \"role\": \"assistant\",\n    \"parts\": [\n      {\n        \"type\": \"text\",\n        \"content\": \"The weather in Paris is currently rainy with a temperature of 57°F.\"\n      }\n    ]\n  }\n]\n"]`.

Attribute annotations:

```json
{
  "qyl": {
    "phase": "end"
  }
}
```

#### Attribute details: `gen_ai.response.finish_reasons`

Values correspond to generations in the same order as the returned
choices/candidates.

Each position SHOULD contain the finish reason for the corresponding
choice/candidate. If a finish reason was expected but not received, for
example because generation failed, was cancelled, or a stream ended before
the final event, instrumentations SHOULD report `error` for that position
instead of omitting it.

`error` indicates that the generation ended abnormally, whether reported
by the provider or inferred by the instrumentation.


Examples: `[["stop"],["stop","length"],["stop","length","error"]]`.

Attribute annotations:

```json
{
  "qyl": {
    "phase": "end"
  }
}
```

Examples: `["chatcmpl-123"]`.

```json
  "qyl": {
    "phase": "end"
  }
}
```

| `error.type` | enum | opt_in | false | stable | Describes a class of error the operation ended with.  The `error.type` SHOULD be predictable, and SHOULD have low cardinality.  When `error.type` is set to a type (e.g., an exception type), its canonical class name identifying the type within the artifact SHOULD be used.  If the recorded error type is a wrapper that is not meaningful for failure classification, instrumentation MAY use the type of the inner error instead. For example, in Go, errors created with `fmt.Errorf` using `%w` MAY be unwrapped when the wrapper type does not help classify the failure.  Instrumentations SHOULD document the list of errors they report.  The cardinality of `error.type` within one instrumentation library SHOULD be low. Telemetry consumers that aggregate data from multiple instrumentation libraries and applications should be prepared for `error.type` to have high cardinality at query time when no additional filters are applied.  If the operation has completed successfully, instrumentations SHOULD NOT set `error.type`.  If a specific domain defines its own set of error identifiers (such as HTTP or RPC status codes), it's RECOMMENDED to:  - Use a domain-specific attribute - Set `error.type` to capture all errors, regardless of whether they are defined within the domain-specific set or not.  |
| `gen_ai.agent.id` | string | opt_in | false | development | The unique and stable identifier of the GenAI hosted agent resource. For hosted agents, this SHOULD be the provider-assigned stable identifier of the agent resource such as [AWS Bedrock agent ARN](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/APIReference/API_agent_Agent.html) or [GCP Agent Registry identifier](https://docs.cloud.google.com/agent-registry/concepts#agent-identifier). It's NOT RECOMMENDED to record in-memory agent instance ids on this attribute due to their transient nature.  |
| `gen_ai.conversation.id` | string | opt_in | false | development | The unique identifier for a conversation (session, thread), used to store and correlate messages within this conversation. Instrumentations SHOULD populate conversation id when they have an identifier for the conversation readily available for a given operation, for example:  - when the client framework being instrumented manages conversation history (see [LlamaIndex chat store](https://docs.llamaindex.ai/en/stable/module_guides/storing/chat_stores/), [LangChain `session_id`](https://reference.langchain.com/python/langchain-core/runnables/history/RunnableWithMessageHistory), and [Google ADK sessions](https://adk.dev/sessions/session)) - when instrumenting GenAI client libraries that maintain a conversation on the backend (see [AWS Bedrock agent sessions](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/agents-session-state.html), [OpenAI Assistant threads](https://platform.openai.com/docs/api-reference/threads))  When no identifier for the conversation is available, instrumentations SHOULD NOT populate conversation id. For example, a new UUID, a trace identifier, or a hash of request content SHOULD NOT be used as a fallback value.  Application developers that manage conversation history MAY add conversation id to GenAI and other spans or logs using custom span or log record processors or hooks provided by instrumentation libraries.  |
| `gen_ai.memory.record.id` | string | opt_in | false | development | The unique identifier of the memory record. |
| `gen_ai.memory.store.id` | string | opt_in | false | development | The unique identifier of the memory store. Semantic conventions for individual components SHOULD document what `gen_ai.memory.store.id` maps to within the implementation.  |
| `gen_ai.provider.name` | enum | opt_in | false | development | The Generative AI provider as identified by the client or server instrumentation. Semantic conventions for individual GenAI operations SHOULD clarify which kinds of providers (e.g. inference, embeddings, retrieval, memory, hosted agent providers) apply when it is not clear from context.  The attribute SHOULD be set based on the instrumentation's best knowledge and may differ from the actual upstream provider. For example, a client SDK may be configured against a proxy or hosting platform that transparently relays requests to a different provider.  The `gen_ai.provider.name` attribute acts as a discriminator that identifies the GenAI telemetry format flavor specific to that provider within GenAI semantic conventions. It SHOULD be set consistently with provider-specific attributes and signals. For example, GenAI spans, metrics, and events related to AWS Bedrock should have the `gen_ai.provider.name` set to `aws.bedrock` and include applicable `aws.bedrock.*` attributes and are not expected to include `openai.*` attributes.  |
| `http.request.method` | enum | opt_in | false | stable | HTTP request method. HTTP request method value SHOULD be "known" to the instrumentation. By default, this convention defines "known" methods as the ones listed in [RFC9110](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9110.html#name-methods), the PATCH method defined in [RFC5789](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc5789.html) and the QUERY method defined in [httpbis-safe-method-w-body](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/draft-ietf-httpbis-safe-method-w-body/?include_text=1).  If the HTTP request method is not known to instrumentation, it MUST set the `http.request.method` attribute to `_OTHER`.  If the HTTP instrumentation could end up converting valid HTTP request methods to `_OTHER`, then it MUST provide a way to override the list of known HTTP methods. If this override is done via environment variable, then the environment variable MUST be named OTEL_INSTRUMENTATION_HTTP_KNOWN_METHODS and support a comma-separated list of case-sensitive known HTTP methods.  ![Development](https://img.shields.io/badge/-development-blue) If this override is done via declarative configuration, then the list MUST be configurable via the `known_methods` property (an array of case-sensitive strings with minimum items 0) under `.instrumentation/development.general.http.client` and/or `.instrumentation/development.general.http.server`.  In either case, this list MUST be a full override of the default known methods, it is not a list of known methods in addition to the defaults.  HTTP method names are case-sensitive and `http.request.method` attribute value MUST match a known HTTP method name exactly. Instrumentations for specific web frameworks that consider HTTP methods to be case insensitive, SHOULD populate a canonical equivalent. Tracing instrumentations that do so, MUST also set `http.request.method_original` to the original value.  |
| `http.request.resend_count` | int | opt_in | false | stable | The ordinal number of request resending attempt (for any reason, including redirects).  The resend count SHOULD be updated each time an HTTP request gets resent by the client, regardless of what was the cause of the resending (e.g. redirection, authorization failure, 503 Server Unavailable, network issues, or any other).  |
| `http.response.status_code` | int | opt_in | false | stable | [HTTP response status code](https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc7231#section-6). |
| `http.route` | string | opt_in | false | stable | The matched route template for the request. This MUST be low-cardinality and include all static path segments, with dynamic path segments represented with placeholders.  MUST NOT be populated when this is not supported by the HTTP server framework as the route attribute should have low-cardinality and the URI path can NOT substitute it. SHOULD include the [application root](/docs/http/http-spans.md#http-server-definitions) if there is one.  A static path segment is a part of the route template with a fixed, low-cardinality value. This includes literal strings like `/users/` and placeholders that are constrained to a finite, predefined set of values, e.g. `{controller}` or `{action}`.  A dynamic path segment is a placeholder for a value that can have high cardinality and is not constrained to a predefined list like static path segments.  Instrumentations SHOULD use routing information provided by the corresponding web framework. They SHOULD pick the most precise source of routing information and MAY support custom route formatting. Instrumentations SHOULD document the format and the API used to obtain the route string.  |
| `server.address` | string | opt_in | false | stable | Server domain name if available without reverse DNS lookup; otherwise, IP address or UNIX domain socket name. When observed from the client side, and when communicating through an intermediary, `server.address` SHOULD represent the server address behind any intermediaries, for example proxies, if it's available.  |
| `server.port` | int | opt_in | false | stable | Server port number. When observed from the client side, and when communicating through an intermediary, `server.port` SHOULD represent the server port behind any intermediaries, for example proxies, if it's available.  |
| `url.full` | string | opt_in | false | stable | Absolute URL describing a network resource according to [RFC3986](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc3986) For network calls, URL usually has `scheme://host[:port][path][?query][#fragment]` format, where the fragment is not transmitted over HTTP, but if it is known, it SHOULD be included nevertheless.  `url.full` MUST NOT contain credentials passed via URL in form of `https://username:password@www.example.com/`. In such case username and password SHOULD be redacted and attribute's value SHOULD be `https://REDACTED:REDACTED@www.example.com/`.  `url.full` SHOULD capture the absolute URL when it is available (or can be reconstructed).  Sensitive content provided in `url.full` SHOULD be scrubbed when instrumentations can identify it.  ![Development](https://img.shields.io/badge/-development-blue) Query string values for the following keys SHOULD be redacted by default and replaced by the value `REDACTED`:  * [`X-Amz-Signature`](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/IAM/latest/UserGuide/reference_sigv-authentication-methods.html) * [`X-Amz-Credential`](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/IAM/latest/UserGuide/reference_sigv-authentication-methods.html) * [`X-Amz-Security-Token`](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/IAM/latest/UserGuide/reference_sigv-authentication-methods.html) * [`sig`](https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/storage/common/storage-sas-overview#sas-token) * [`X-Goog-Signature`](https://cloud.google.com/storage/docs/access-control/signed-urls)  This list is subject to change over time.  Matching of query parameter keys against the sensitive list SHOULD be case-sensitive.  ![Development](https://img.shields.io/badge/-development-blue) Instrumentation MAY provide a way to override this list via declarative configuration. If so, it SHOULD use the `sensitive_query_parameters` property (an array of case-sensitive strings with minimum items 0) under `.instrumentation/development.general.sanitization.url`. This list is a full override of the default sensitive query parameter keys, it is not a list of keys in addition to the defaults. If the HTTP instrumentation could end up converting valid HTTP request methods to `_OTHER`, then it MUST provide a way to override the list of known HTTP methods. For example, a new UUID, a trace identifier, or a hash of request content SHOULD NOT be used as a fallback value.  Application developers that manage conversation history MAY add conversation id to GenAI and other spans or logs using custom span or log record processors or hooks provided by instrumentation libraries.  |

| `gen_ai.tool.call.id` | string | opt_in | false | development | The tool call identifier supplied by the model or provider. This attribute SHOULD be set to the identifier received from the model or provider if and only if one was supplied.  |
| `gen_ai.tool.description` | string | opt_in | false | development | The tool description. > [!WARNING] > This attribute may contain sensitive information.  |
| `gen_ai.tool.name` | string | opt_in | false | development | Name of the tool utilized by the agent. |
| `gen_ai.tool.type` | string | opt_in | false | development | Type of the tool utilized by the agent Extension: A tool executed on the agent-side to directly call external APIs, bridging the gap between the agent and real-world systems.   Agent-side operations involve actions that are performed by the agent on the server or within the agent's controlled environment. Function: A tool executed on the client-side, where the agent generates parameters for a predefined function, and the client executes the logic.   Client-side operations are actions taken on the user's end or within the client application. Datastore: A tool used by the agent to access and query structured or unstructured external data for retrieval-augmented tasks or knowledge updates.  |

Instrumentations MAY provide a way for users to filter or truncate output messages. `gen_ai.response.finish_reasons` remains aligned with the generations returned by the provider, not with a filtered or truncated `gen_ai.output.messages` value. | `http.request.method` | enum | opt_in | false | stable | HTTP request method. HTTP request method value SHOULD be "known" to the instrumentation. By default, this convention defines "known" methods as the ones listed in [RFC9110](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9110.html#name-methods), the PATCH method defined in [RFC5789](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc5789.html) and the QUERY method defined in [httpbis-safe-method-w-body](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/draft-ietf-httpbis-safe-method-w-body/?include_text=1).  If the HTTP request method is not known to instrumentation, it MUST set the `http.request.method` attribute to `_OTHER`.  If the HTTP instrumentation could end up converting valid HTTP request methods to `_OTHER`, then it MUST provide a way to override the list of known HTTP methods. If this override is done via environment variable, then the environment variable MUST be named OTEL_INSTRUMENTATION_HTTP_KNOWN_METHODS and support a comma-separated list of case-sensitive known HTTP methods.  ![Development](https://img.shields.io/badge/-development-blue) If this override is done via declarative configuration, then the list MUST be configurable via the `known_methods` property (an array of case-sensitive strings with minimum items 0) under `.instrumentation/development.general.http.client` and/or `.instrumentation/development.general.http.server`.  In either case, this list MUST be a full override of the default known methods, it is not a list of known methods in addition to the defaults.  HTTP method names are case-sensitive and `http.request.method` attribute value MUST match a known HTTP method name exactly. Instrumentations for specific web frameworks that consider HTTP methods to be case insensitive, SHOULD populate a canonical equivalent. Tracing instrumentations that do so, MUST also set `http.request.method_original` to the original value.  |
| `http.response.status_code` | int | opt_in | false | stable | [HTTP response status code](https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc7231#section-6). |
| `http.route` | string | opt_in | false | stable | The matched route template for the request. This MUST be low-cardinality and include all static path segments, with dynamic path segments represented with placeholders.  MUST NOT be populated when this is not supported by the HTTP server framework as the route attribute should have low-cardinality and the URI path can NOT substitute it. SHOULD include the [application root](/docs/http/http-spans.md#http-server-definitions) if there is one.  A static path segment is a part of the route template with a fixed, low-cardinality value. This includes literal strings like `/users/` and placeholders that are constrained to a finite, predefined set of values, e.g. `{controller}` or `{action}`.  A dynamic path segment is a placeholder for a value that can have high cardinality and is not constrained to a predefined list like static path segments.  Instrumentations SHOULD use routing information provided by the corresponding web framework. They SHOULD pick the most precise source of routing information and MAY support custom route formatting. Instrumentations SHOULD document the format and the API used to obtain the route string.  |
| `server.address` | string | opt_in | false | stable | Server domain name if available without reverse DNS lookup; otherwise, IP address or UNIX domain socket name. | `server.port` | int | opt_in | false | stable | Server port number. When observed from the client side, and when communicating through an intermediary, `server.port` SHOULD represent the server port behind any intermediaries, for example proxies, if it's available.  |
| `url.full` | string | opt_in | false | stable | Absolute URL describing a network resource according to [RFC3986](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc3986) For network calls, URL usually has `scheme://host[:port][path][?query][#fragment]` format, where the fragment is not transmitted over HTTP, but if it is known, it SHOULD be included nevertheless.  `url.full` MUST NOT contain credentials passed via URL in form of `https://username:password@www.example.com/`. In such case username and password SHOULD be redacted and attribute's value SHOULD be `https://REDACTED:REDACTED@www.example.com/`.  `url.full` SHOULD capture the absolute URL when it is available (or can be reconstructed).  Sensitive content provided in `url.full` SHOULD be scrubbed when instrumentations can identify it.  ![Development](https://img.shields.io/badge/-development-blue) Query string values for the following keys SHOULD be redacted by default and replaced by the value `REDACTED`:  * [`X-Amz-Signature`](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/IAM/latest/UserGuide/reference_sigv-authentication-methods.html) * [`X-Amz-Credential`](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/IAM/latest/UserGuide/reference_sigv-authentication-methods.html) * [`X-Amz-Security-Token`](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/IAM/latest/UserGuide/reference_sigv-authentication-methods.html) * [`sig`](https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/storage/common/storage-sas-overview#sas-token) * [`X-Goog-Signature`](https://cloud.google.com/storage/docs/access-control/signed-urls)  This list is subject to change over time.  Matching of query parameter keys against the sensitive list SHOULD be case-sensitive.  ![Development](https://img.shields.io/badge/-development-blue) Instrumentation MAY provide a way to override this list via declarative configuration. If so, it SHOULD use the `sensitive_query_parameters` property (an array of case-sensitive strings with minimum items 0) under `.instrumentation/development.general.sanitization.url`. | `url.path` | string | opt_in | false | stable | The [URI path](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc3986#section-3.3) component  Sensitive content provided in `url.path` SHOULD be scrubbed when instrumentations can identify it.  |
| `url.query` | string | opt_in | false | stable | The [URI query](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc3986#section-3.4) component  Sensitive content provided in `url.query` SHOULD be scrubbed when instrumentations can identify it.  ![Development](https://img.shields.io/badge/-development-blue) Query string values for the following keys SHOULD be redacted by default and replaced by the value `REDACTED`:  * [`X-Amz-Signature`](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/IAM/latest/UserGuide/reference_sigv-authentication-methods.html) * [`X-Amz-Credential`](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/IAM/latest/UserGuide/reference_sigv-authentication-methods.html) * [`X-Amz-Security-Token`](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/IAM/latest/UserGuide/reference_sigv-authentication-methods.html) * [`sig`](https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/storage/common/storage-sas-overview#sas-token) * [`X-Goog-Signature`](https://cloud.google.com/storage/docs/access-control/signed-urls)  This list is subject to change over time.  Matching of query parameter keys against the sensitive list SHOULD be case-sensitive.  Instrumentation MAY provide a way to override this list via declarative configuration. This list is a full override of the default sensitive query parameter keys, it is not a list of keys in addition to the defaults.  When a query string value is redacted, the query string key SHOULD still be preserved, e.g. `q=OpenTelemetry&sig=REDACTED`.  |

| `gen_ai.usage.input_tokens` | int | opt_in | false | development | The number of tokens used in the GenAI input (prompt). This value SHOULD include all types of input tokens, including cached tokens. Instrumentations SHOULD make a best effort to populate this value, using a total provided by the provider when available or, depending on the provider API, by summing different token types parsed from the provider output.  When the provider reports both billed token counts and model-consumed token counts (for example, Cohere exposes both `usage.billed_units` and `usage.tokens`), instrumentations SHOULD report the billed count so the value matches the units the customer is charged for.  Detailed usage attributes are subsets of total and aggregate counts. For example, if a request has 100 text tokens (40 cached) and 200 image tokens: - `gen_ai.usage.input_tokens`: 300 - `gen_ai.usage.cache_read.input_tokens`: 40 - `gen_ai.usage.text.input_tokens`: 100 - `gen_ai.usage.text.cache_read.input_tokens`: 40 - `gen_ai.usage.image.input_tokens`: 200  |
| `gen_ai.usage.output_tokens` | int | opt_in | false | development | The number of tokens used in the GenAI response (completion). When the provider reports both billed token counts and model-consumed token counts (for example, Cohere exposes both `usage.billed_units` and `usage.tokens`), instrumentations SHOULD report the billed count so the value matches the units the customer is charged for.  |

| `error.type` | enum | opt_in | false | stable | Describes a class of error the operation ended with.  The `error.type` SHOULD be predictable, and SHOULD have low cardinality.  When `error.type` is set to a type (e.g., an exception type), its canonical class name identifying the type within the artifact SHOULD be used.  If the recorded error type is a wrapper that is not meaningful for failure classification, instrumentation MAY use the type of the inner error instead. For example, in Go, errors created with `fmt.Errorf` using `%w` MAY be unwrapped when the wrapper type does not help classify the failure.  Instrumentations SHOULD document the list of errors they report.  The cardinality of `error.type` within one instrumentation library SHOULD be low. Telemetry consumers that aggregate data from multiple instrumentation libraries and applications should be prepared for `error.type` to have high cardinality at query time when no additional filters are applied.  If the operation has completed successfully, instrumentations SHOULD NOT set `error.type`.  If a specific domain defines its own set of error identifiers (such as HTTP or RPC status codes), it's RECOMMENDED to:  - Use a domain-specific attribute - Set `error.type` to capture all errors, regardless of whether they are defined within the domain-specific set or not.  |
| `gen_ai.conversation.id` | string | opt_in | false | development | The unique identifier for a conversation (session, thread), used to store and correlate messages within this conversation. Instrumentations SHOULD populate conversation id when they have an identifier for the conversation readily available for a given operation, for example:  - when the client framework being instrumented manages conversation history (see [LlamaIndex chat store](https://docs.llamaindex.ai/en/stable/module_guides/storing/chat_stores/), [LangChain `session_id`](https://reference.langchain.com/python/langchain-core/runnables/history/RunnableWithMessageHistory), and [Google ADK sessions](https://adk.dev/sessions/session)) - when instrumenting GenAI client libraries that maintain a conversation on the backend (see [AWS Bedrock agent sessions](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/agents-session-state.html), [OpenAI Assistant threads](https://platform.openai.com/docs/api-reference/threads))  When no identifier for the conversation is available, instrumentations SHOULD NOT populate conversation id. For example, a new UUID, a trace identifier, or a hash of request content SHOULD NOT be used as a fallback value.  Application developers that manage conversation history MAY add conversation id to GenAI and other spans or logs using custom span or log record processors or hooks provided by instrumentation libraries.  |
| `gen_ai.provider.name` | enum | opt_in | false | development | The Generative AI provider as identified by the client or server instrumentation. Semantic conventions for individual GenAI operations SHOULD clarify which kinds of providers (e.g. inference, embeddings, retrieval, memory, hosted agent providers) apply when it is not clear from context.  The attribute SHOULD be set based on the instrumentation's best knowledge and may differ from the actual upstream provider. For example, a client SDK may be configured against a proxy or hosting platform that transparently relays requests to a different provider.  The `gen_ai.provider.name` attribute acts as a discriminator that identifies the GenAI telemetry format flavor specific to that provider within GenAI semantic conventions. It SHOULD be set consistently with provider-specific attributes and signals. For example, GenAI spans, metrics, and events related to AWS Bedrock should have the `gen_ai.provider.name` set to `aws.bedrock` and include applicable `aws.bedrock.*` attributes and are not expected to include `openai.*` attributes.  |
| `http.request.method` | enum | opt_in | false | stable | HTTP request method. HTTP request method value SHOULD be "known" to the instrumentation. By default, this convention defines "known" methods as the ones listed in [RFC9110](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9110.html#name-methods), the PATCH method defined in [RFC5789](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc5789.html) and the QUERY method defined in [httpbis-safe-method-w-body](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/draft-ietf-httpbis-safe-method-w-body/?include_text=1).  If the HTTP request method is not known to instrumentation, it MUST set the `http.request.method` attribute to `_OTHER`.  If the HTTP instrumentation could end up converting valid HTTP request methods to `_OTHER`, then it MUST provide a way to override the list of known HTTP methods. If this override is done via environment variable, then the environment variable MUST be named OTEL_INSTRUMENTATION_HTTP_KNOWN_METHODS and support a comma-separated list of case-sensitive known HTTP methods.  ![Development](https://img.shields.io/badge/-development-blue) If this override is done via declarative configuration, then the list MUST be configurable via the `known_methods` property (an array of case-sensitive strings with minimum items 0) under `.instrumentation/development.general.http.client` and/or `.instrumentation/development.general.http.server`.  In either case, this list MUST be a full override of the default known methods, it is not a list of known methods in addition to the defaults.  HTTP method names are case-sensitive and `http.request.method` attribute value MUST match a known HTTP method name exactly. Instrumentations for specific web frameworks that consider HTTP methods to be case insensitive, SHOULD populate a canonical equivalent. Tracing instrumentations that do so, MUST also set `http.request.method_original` to the original value.  |
| `http.response.status_code` | int | opt_in | false | stable | [HTTP response status code](https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc7231#section-6). |
| `http.route` | string | opt_in | false | stable | The matched route template for the request. This MUST be low-cardinality and include all static path segments, with dynamic path segments represented with placeholders.  MUST NOT be populated when this is not supported by the HTTP server framework as the route attribute should have low-cardinality and the URI path can NOT substitute it. SHOULD include the [application root](/docs/http/http-spans.md#http-server-definitions) if there is one.  A static path segment is a part of the route template with a fixed, low-cardinality value. This includes literal strings like `/users/` and placeholders that are constrained to a finite, predefined set of values, e.g. `{controller}` or `{action}`.  A dynamic path segment is a placeholder for a value that can have high cardinality and is not constrained to a predefined list like static path segments.  Instrumentations SHOULD use routing information provided by the corresponding web framework. They SHOULD pick the most precise source of routing information and MAY support custom route formatting. Instrumentations SHOULD document the format and the API used to obtain the route string.  |
| `server.address` | string | opt_in | false | stable | Server domain name if available without reverse DNS lookup; otherwise, IP address or UNIX domain socket name. When observed from the client side, and when communicating through an intermediary, `server.address` SHOULD represent the server address behind any intermediaries, for example proxies, if it's available.  |
| `server.port` | int | opt_in | false | stable | Server port number. When observed from the client side, and when communicating through an intermediary, `server.port` SHOULD represent the server port behind any intermediaries, for example proxies, if it's available.  |
| `url.full` | string | opt_in | false | stable | Absolute URL describing a network resource according to [RFC3986](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc3986) For network calls, URL usually has `scheme://host[:port][path][?query][#fragment]` format, where the fragment is not transmitted over HTTP, but if it is known, it SHOULD be included nevertheless.  `url.full` MUST NOT contain credentials passed via URL in form of `https://username:password@www.example.com/`. In such case username and password SHOULD be redacted and attribute's value SHOULD be `https://REDACTED:REDACTED@www.example.com/`.  `url.full` SHOULD capture the absolute URL when it is available (or can be reconstructed).  Sensitive content provided in `url.full` SHOULD be scrubbed when instrumentations can identify it.  ![Development](https://img.shields.io/badge/-development-blue) Query string values for the following keys SHOULD be redacted by default and replaced by the value `REDACTED`:  * [`X-Amz-Signature`](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/IAM/latest/UserGuide/reference_sigv-authentication-methods.html) * [`X-Amz-Credential`](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/IAM/latest/UserGuide/reference_sigv-authentication-methods.html) * [`X-Amz-Security-Token`](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/IAM/latest/UserGuide/reference_sigv-authentication-methods.html) * [`sig`](https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/storage/common/storage-sas-overview#sas-token) * [`X-Goog-Signature`](https://cloud.google.com/storage/docs/access-control/signed-urls)  This list is subject to change over time.  Matching of query parameter keys against the sensitive list SHOULD be case-sensitive.  ![Development](https://img.shields.io/badge/-development-blue) Instrumentation MAY provide a way to override this list via declarative configuration. ### metric.vendor.microsoft_extensions_ai.gen_ai_client_token_usage

| Property | Definition |

| Stability | development |

| metric_name | `gen_ai.client.token.usage` |
| instrument | `histogram` |

The histogram semantic-conventions-genai carried until 8ffdf56 (#374) replaced it with the `gen_ai.client.inference.usage.*` counters and the `gen_ai.client.inference.operation.{input,output}_tokens` histograms. Created by `OtelMetricHelpers.CreateGenAITokenUsageHistogram` at src/Libraries/Microsoft.Extensions.AI/Common/OtelMetricHelpers.cs:12-17 from the name at src/Libraries/Microsoft.Extensions.AI/OpenTelemetryConsts.cs:71, on the Meter of every decorator listed on `gen_ai.token.type`; recorded at src/Libraries/Microsoft.Extensions.AI/ChatCompletion/OpenTelemetryChatClient.cs:424,432 as one measurement per token type.

| Attribute | Type | Requirement / role | Sampling relevant | Stability | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `gen_ai.operation.name` | enum | required | Not applicable | development | The name of the operation being performed. If one of the predefined values applies, but specific system uses a different name it's RECOMMENDED to document it in the semantic conventions for specific GenAI system and use system-specific name in the instrumentation. If a different name is not documented, instrumentation libraries SHOULD use applicable predefined value.  |
| `gen_ai.provider.name` | enum | required | Not applicable | development | The Generative AI provider as identified by the client or server instrumentation. Semantic conventions for individual GenAI operations SHOULD clarify which kinds of providers (e.g. inference, embeddings, retrieval, memory, hosted agent providers) apply when it is not clear from context.  The attribute SHOULD be set based on the instrumentation's best knowledge and may differ from the actual upstream provider. For example, a client SDK may be configured against a proxy or hosting platform that transparently relays requests to a different provider.  The `gen_ai.provider.name` attribute acts as a discriminator that identifies the GenAI telemetry format flavor specific to that provider within GenAI semantic conventions. It SHOULD be set consistently with provider-specific attributes and signals. For example, GenAI spans, metrics, and events related to AWS Bedrock should have the `gen_ai.provider.name` set to `aws.bedrock` and include applicable `aws.bedrock.*` attributes and are not expected to include `openai.*` attributes.  |
| `gen_ai.request.model` | string | {"conditionally_required":"If available."} | Not applicable | development | The name of the GenAI model a request is being made to. |
| `gen_ai.response.model` | string | recommended | Not applicable | development | The name of the model that generated the response. |
| `gen_ai.token.type` | enum | required | Not applicable | development | The type of token `gen_ai.client.token.usage` counts, as Microsoft.Extensions.AI 10.10.0 spells it. Metric tag on the "Experimental.Microsoft.Extensions.AI" Meter, the dimension of `gen_ai.client.token.usage`. Declared as `OpenTelemetryConsts.GenAI.Token.Type` at src/Libraries/Microsoft.Extensions.AI/OpenTelemetryConsts.cs:149 with its values at :26-31; set at src/Libraries/Microsoft.Extensions.AI/ChatCompletion/OpenTelemetryChatClient.cs:422,430, src/Libraries/Microsoft.Extensions.AI/Embeddings/OpenTelemetryEmbeddingGenerator.cs:216, src/Libraries/Microsoft.Extensions.AI/ChatCompletion/OpenTelemetryImageGenerator.cs:247,255, src/Libraries/Microsoft.Extensions.AI/SpeechToText/OpenTelemetrySpeechToTextClient.cs:266,274, src/Libraries/Microsoft.Extensions.AI/TextToSpeech/OpenTelemetryTextToSpeechClient.cs:265,273 and, for all six members, src/Libraries/Microsoft.Extensions.AI/Realtime/OpenTelemetryRealtimeClientSession.cs:764-804. Upstream semantic-conventions-genai 8ffdf56 (#374) replaced the key with `gen_ai.token.modality`, whose values are modalities rather than directions; the two are different keys and neither is a rename of the other. |
| `server.address` | string | recommended | Not applicable | stable | Server domain name if available without reverse DNS lookup; otherwise, IP address or UNIX domain socket name. When observed from the client side, and when communicating through an intermediary, `server.address` SHOULD represent the server address behind any intermediaries, for example proxies, if it's available.  |
| `server.port` | int | {"conditionally_required":"If `server.address` is set."} | Not applicable | stable | Server port number. When observed from the client side, and when communicating through an intermediary, `server.port` SHOULD represent the server port behind any intermediaries, for example proxies, if it's available.  |

### metric.vendor.openai_codex.codex.agents_md.edit

Counts/accumulates agents md edit observations; interpret each dimension using the source.

| Property | Definition |
| --- | --- |
| Kind | `metric` |
| Stability | development |
| Signal collection | recommended |
| metric_name | `codex.agents_md.edit` |
| instrument | `counter` |
| unit | Empty on the native instrument |
| Registry schema | https://qyl.at/schemas/15.0.1 |
| Source | `registry/vendor/openai-codex.yaml` |

The native instrument omits OTLP unit metadata. The empty unit is intentional; a unit inferred from the name must not be presented as an emitted unit.

Value semantics: counter / count/value; see meaning. Counters accumulate nonnegative increments; histograms observe values; gauges report current observations. Native dimensions are source-defined strings. Session wrappers can add shared tags, but they are not required on process-global instruments.

https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/rust-v0.163.0/codex-rs/core/src/tools/runtimes/apply_patch.rs#L222

Metric API and unit construction: https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/rust-v0.163.0/codex-rs/otel/src/metrics/client.rs#L117

| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `filename` | string | recommended | Not applicable | development | Native filename field emitted by the pinned Codex runtime. String-valued native metric dimension. Do not promote unbounded diagnostic values or session IDs into additional metric dimensions. |

Operation boundary: the lifetime of the source tracing span or instrumented function/future, including an early return or cancellation. It does not imply the lifetime of a whole conversation or a successful remote operation. The source name is agents_md.load; explicit exported names: agents_md.load.

Span kind: internal by the tracing OpenTelemetry default. Preserve a recorded status. Do not infer native error status merely because a log or error.message exists. Values declared as field::Empty arrive only if the source later records them; they are unavailable for head sampling before that point. Client peer address/port, where not recorded by the producer, remain unavailable rather than fabricated.

Span kind: internal by the tracing OpenTelemetry default. Preserve a recorded status. Do not infer native error status merely because a log or error.message exists. Values declared as field::Empty arrive only if the source later records them; they are unavailable for head sampling before that point. Client peer address/port, where not recorded by the producer, remain unavailable rather than fabricated.

https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/rust-v0.163.0/codex-rs/core/src/unified_exec/process_manager.rs#L865

### registry.vendor.oracle_data_provider_for_net_odp_net_core

Attributes ODP.NET Core puts on the spans of its own "Oracle.ManagedDataAccess.Core" ActivitySource and that upstream semantic conventions 1.44.0 does not define. This is the one vendor model whose finding is a vendor document rather than source at a tag: the provider is closed-source.

| Property | Definition |
| --- | --- |
| Kind | `attribute_group` |
| Stability | Defined per attribute |
| Registry schema | https://qyl.at/schemas/15.0.1 |
| Source | `registry/vendor/oracle-data-provider-for-net-odp-net-core.yaml` |

| Attribute | Type | Requirement / role | Sampling relevant | Stability | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `db.odp.connection.id` | string | recommended | Not applicable | development | Unique identifier of the ODP.NET connection, for diagnostic purposes. |
| `db.odp.roundtrip.count` | int | recommended | Not applicable | development | Number of database server roundtrips the ODP.NET method makes. |
| `db.odp.roundtrip.duration` | string | recommended | Not applicable | development | Database server roundtrip time, including ODP.NET processing, network send and receive, and database server processing. |
| `db.odp.rows_affected` | int | recommended | Not applicable | development | Row count affected by the SQL DML statement. |
| `db.odp.sql_id` | string | recommended | Not applicable | development | Oracle database SQL statement identifier, equivalent to SQL_ID. |
| `db.odp.user.statement` | string | recommended | Not applicable | development | Redacted ODP.NET user-supplied command text, which can differ from the statement the database executes. |

#### Attribute details: `db.odp.connection.id`

Span tag on the "Oracle.ManagedDataAccess.Core" ActivitySource. ODP.NET ships no public source, so the finding is the vendor's own attribute table in Oracle's ODP.NET OpenTelemetry documentation, https://docs.oracle.com/en/database/oracle/oracle-database/23/odpnt/featOpenTelemetry.html; the brief is that table's wording and the type follows the fact it describes.

Examples: `["lVd4L7ekiU2z0QXMF+WT6A==","OrderSvc4Svv2bWEAmXgYwIAAH/2Bw=="]`.

#### Attribute details: `db.odp.roundtrip.count`

Span tag on the "Oracle.ManagedDataAccess.Core" ActivitySource. ODP.NET ships no public source, so the finding is the vendor's own attribute table in Oracle's ODP.NET OpenTelemetry documentation, https://docs.oracle.com/en/database/oracle/oracle-database/23/odpnt/featOpenTelemetry.html; the brief is that table's wording and the type follows the fact it describes.

#### Attribute details: `db.odp.roundtrip.duration`

Oracle documents the duration's meaning at https://docs.oracle.com/en/database/oracle/oracle-database/23/odpnt/featOpenTelemetry.html, without declaring a numeric wire type or unit. The pinned 23.26.301 provider exposes a System.TimeSpan Activity tag; real OTLP capture with SDK 1.20.0 preserves it as a duration string, for example 00:00:00.0595180. Keep that representation; do not invent a numeric unit.

Examples: `["00:00:00.0595180"]`.

#### Attribute details: `db.odp.rows_affected`

Span tag on the "Oracle.ManagedDataAccess.Core" ActivitySource. ODP.NET ships no public source, so the finding is the vendor's own attribute table in Oracle's ODP.NET OpenTelemetry documentation, https://docs.oracle.com/en/database/oracle/oracle-database/23/odpnt/featOpenTelemetry.html; the brief is that table's wording and the type follows the fact it describes.
